question_papers.paper_title: Set 1 - Nature’s Treasures NCERT Practice Paper

questions.question_text: Valuable substances provided by nature to sustain life are:
Key primary natural treasures on Earth include:
questions.correct_answer: B) Pure Air, Fresh Water, Soil, Sunlight

questions.question_text: Dark organic soil layer formed by decomposing leaf litter is:
Washing away of fertile topsoil by heavy rain or wind is:
Forest tree networks prevent topsoil erosion because:
Define key concept set 1 related to Nature’s Treasures.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Core scientific definition derived from NCERT Chapter 11 curriculum guidelines.

questions.question_text: Differentiate between two fundamental processes in Chapter 11.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Point 1: Physical / Structural distinction. Point 2: Functional / Practical difference.

questions.question_text: State two practical real-life applications of principles from Nature’s Treasures.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Daily utility in home/kitchen/nature. 2. Environmental or technological benefit.

questions.question_text: Explain the step-by-step procedure of an experiment in Chapter 11.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Materials required. 2. Experimental procedure steps. 3. Final observation and scientific conclusion.

questions.question_text: Give scientific reasons for an observed natural phenomenon in Nature’s Treasures.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Detailed reasoning connecting physical properties or biological adaptations with environmental conditions.

questions.question_text:
Case Scenario Set 1: Students observe a practical situation related to Nature’s Treasures.
(a) Identify the core problem or variable. (1 Mark)
(b) Explain the underlying scientific mechanism. (2 Marks)
(c) Suggest a testable solution or precaution. (1 Mark)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(a) Correct identification of variable.
(b) Scientific explanation connecting causes with effects.
(c) Practical precaution or verified solution.

questions.question_text:
Assertion-Reason Question Set 1:
Assertion (A): Scientific principle holds true under tested conditions in Chapter 11.
Reason (R): Evidence gathered from experiments supports the conclusion.
Options: (a) Both A and R are true, and R explains A. (b) Both true, but R does not explain A. (c) A true, R false. (d) Both false.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: (a) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
